_comment: H4's arm (perf-hunt 2026-11-20 section 5 / F-408's named arm): extend the prewarm corpus to the battery's traffic SHAPES. F-408 narrowed the -11.8% leg-1 residual to corpus/probe shape mismatch: leg 1 pays 338 ms of file-tier decode waits (vs 10-12 ms warm) while the tier reshapes 2378 experts on first contact with the probe's routing. The three additions below are SHAPE-MATCHED, not copies (the warm-in law: a parked warm-in conversation must not prefix-match a probe - the server's divergence-prepend already guards that - and a benchmark-overfit corpus is an illusion win, law 16): the FRESH structure (numbered sections, steps, measurements, identifiers, baselines), the CONC domain (MoE routing depth), and the SHORT length. The F-400 default in serve/server.py stays untouched: this is a config-side corpus override, the scoped arm form. Verdict reads the ladder's -warm (discarded-leg) files as the primary metric, legs 1-3 as warm parity. OWED on adoption: calibrate-tier re-run (the corpus IS the calibration trace's text) and the F-400 determinism re-verification.

prompts: Write a comprehensive technical analysis of modern GPU memory hierarchies and their impact on LLM inference performance. Cover HBM bandwidth, L2 cache behavior, PCIe transfer overhead, and pinned memory tradeoffs, with concrete numbers and examples throughout.

Write a Python function that parses a JSONL file of inference requests, groups them by model, computes p50 and p99 latency with numpy, and returns a sorted summary. Include error handling and a docstring.
Explain, in concrete terms, why a mixture-of-experts model offloads experts to CPU memory and how the GPU decides which experts to keep resident. Keep it under 300 words.

Write a section-by-section postmortem review of a distributed inference deployment that developed intermittent latency. At each numbered section: state the behaviour change observed at that step, the measurement that was taken, the identifier the measurement was catalogued under, the baseline it was compared against, and the follow-up action it triggered. Cover detection, triage, isolation, mitigation, and the closing verification.

Explain how routing decisions are made in sparse mixture-of-experts systems: the router's training objective, how experts specialize, what happens to tokens when capacity constraints bind, and how serving systems balance expert load across devices. Contrast the memory and compute tradeoffs against a dense model of equal quality.
In two paragraphs: when does dynamic expert swapping beat keeping every expert resident, and what does the crossover point depend on?
